label: nokotodakara
title_raw: のことだから [のことだから] (nokotodakara)
title: のことだから
meaning_example: Hiroko as usual, will be late.

notes.text:
〜のことだから　：〜という特徴のある．．．だから．．．（〜と予想される）

              Since it's (someone who...), therefore it is natural to have (someone).... 



〜ことから　：　〜という理由で

               Since ....

examples.japanese: 弘子のことだから、遅れるでしょう.
examples.body_text:
弘子のことだから、遅れるでしょう.  

		Hiroko as usual will be late.

Hiroko as usual will be late.

examples.japanese: あなたのことだから上々でしょう。
examples.body_text:
あなたのことだから上々でしょう。 

		I know you did great!
examples.body_html:
あなたのことだから上々でしょう。 
I know you did great!

comments.text: so wait, is this like の then こと and then （だ）から？ like the thing of the subject and then dakara? Is that what this is like but contains a meaning of 'as usual'?

comments.text: My grammar book, 500 Essential Japanese Expressions: A Guide to Correct Usage of Key Sentence Patterns, has [のことだから], [ことだから], and [ことだ] meaning the same thing: [なのだから].
comments.html: My grammar book, 500 Essential Japanese Expressions: A Guide to Correct Usage of Key Sentence Patterns, has [のことだから], [ことだから], and [ことだ] meaning the same thing: [なのだから].

comments.text: When I took JLPT 2級 they tested the difference between [ことから] and [ことだから]. It is quite easy to mix them up.
comments.html: When I took JLPT 2級 they tested the difference between [ことから] and [ことだから]. It is quite easy to mix them up.

comments.text: This came up several times in something I was translating. I translated "a-san no kotodesukara..." as "It's a-san so...". It seems more natural than saying "A-san as usual...". For example in the example sentence above saying "It's Hiroko so she'll be late" or "Since it's Hiroko she'll be late" might be more natural.
